title: Practice one familiar strength movement with fixed technique and recovery
goal: Understand major strength patterns and use a bounded, technically controlled practice-and-review cycle rather than increasing load simply to prove effort.
scope_note: This is an introductory observation of one already-safe movement, not a universal strength program, rehabilitation plan or demonstration of strength gain. Novel or medically constrained training needs appropriate instruction.
burden: Fifteen minutes of planning and two short sessions on separate suitable days with recovery between them.
setup: Map five movement functions: getting up or squatting, hinging, pushing, pulling and carrying. Choose one familiar, pain-free function already within your ordinary ability or existing qualified plan. Default for someone who routinely stands from a chair: three slow sit-to-stands from a stable chair that cannot slide, using the usual hand support. There is no requirement to remove support, add weight or approach fatigue.

actions.title: Choose the function and define observable technique
actions.instructions: Give each of the five functions a safe current example, an adapted equivalent or an instruction-needed status. Select only one for this trial. For the chair default, use the same stable seat and footwear, keep the movement controlled, use necessary support and stop before technique changes. Record a modest repetition count, rest arrangement and stop conditions; chest symptoms, faintness, new pain or unusual breathlessness stop the attempt.
checks: All five functions receive an example adaptation or instruction-needed status
The selected movement is familiar and appropriate to current ability
Technique support repetitions and recovery are specified before starting
Concerning symptoms or technique loss override the target

actions.title: Complete the bounded session without chasing a maximum
actions.instructions: Perform only the planned repetitions at a comfortable pace, breathing normally and retaining the chosen support. Record repetitions completed with the fixed technique, perceived effort and any symptoms; incomplete repetitions remain incomplete. Stop at the preset boundary even if comparison or enthusiasm suggests adding more. A qualified coach or therapist may observe with consent, but public recording and competitive testing are unnecessary.
checks: Only the preplanned familiar movement and repetitions are attempted
Required support and ordinary breathing are maintained
Completed repetitions require the fixed technique
No maximum load fatigue challenge or unplanned escalation is added

actions.title: Repeat after recovery and choose a justified next step
actions.instructions: At the next suitable session, first check return to usual function and any delayed symptoms. Repeat the same dose only when appropriate under the existing plan. Compare control, effort and recovery, not merely count. Keep the dose, reduce it or ask for instruction; any future progression changes one variable within qualified or established guidance. Two sessions do not establish measurable strength improvement.
checks: Usual function and delayed symptoms are checked before repeating
The repeat uses comparable technique support and dose
Control effort and recovery inform the decision
Progression is conditional and no strength-gain claim is inferred

adaptation: Use a seated, assisted or prescribed equivalent and count support as a legitimate condition. If the default movement is not already safe and familiar, complete the pattern map and obtain instruction before physical attempts. Do not practice through injury, remove fall supports or alter a rehabilitation plan.
review: What evidence supports repeating or changing this dose while preserving technique and recovery?

examples.supportive: Three supported chair rises were controlled on both days with normal recovery, so the same dose was retained provisionally.
examples.mixed: Repetitions were completed, but later discomfort meant the second session was deferred for appropriate advice.
examples.contradictory: Support was removed and repetitions forced through pain to make the result look stronger.
examples.inconclusive: A strength plan was written without a safe attempt or any observation of technique and recovery.
